dumpAndCut.normalDumps: Nominal dumps reach about -2.1 deg and never pass -3.5 deg. Adverse dumps (command -4.29 deg in the pan frame at +0.04 rad pitch) sit below -3.5 deg for 1.83 s in the pan sim and 0.96 s in the return, and touch the soft stop (2.1 N m, min -5.03 deg).
dumpAndCut.directionalCut: Never trips in normal operation: below -3.5 deg the controller commands closing torque against about 3 N m of opening gravity, so there is no opening output to cut. Results are identical to the no-cut control C4.
dumpAndCut.nonDirectionalCut: If the hardware cut removes all drive output (or latches), every adverse case fails reset: the pan coasts onto the soft stop and cannot lift itself back above -3.5 deg. 6/12 resets met.
dumpAndCut.requirement: Implement the -3.5 deg limit as a reverse-direction limit only (non-latching), or move the commanded dump so adverse pitch keeps the pan above -3.5 deg.

driveFault.conclusion: Package F1 reproduced: 57.4 N m soft-stop torque, 319 N per pad, 0.087 strain, -5.67 deg, and 4.74 N m gearbox output after the cut at pad impact. The F1 PEAK gearbox torque is 14.30 N m BEFORE the cut (30 A cap accelerating the pan, eta=1), 8.07 N m with the registered 9 V / eta 0.6 law; both exceed 7.1 N m. The post-cut value scales with the unmeasured rotor inertia: 8.70 N m at 6e-6 and 12.07 N m at 9e-6 kg m2. F2/F3 still reach 0.38/0.45 pad strain and 21.7/25.9 N m.

result.scope: Analytic gravity demand for the listed rigid members about one fixed axis. A stop mean assumes release from rest and only gravity work. Moving disable, achieved clearance, peak loads and installed holding capacity require separate evidence.

rotaryReview.note: stow holding with article -0.562 N m (closes onto the stow stop); at -2 deg the empty pan gravity opens with 3.03 N m

limits: One-plane rigid pan about a fixed pivot; stop is a lumped linear spring-damper (no pad nonlinearity, set, temperature or wear).
Power loss modeled as zero motor torque only; NEO 550 brake-mode, gearbox back-drive friction and controller reboot behaviour are not modeled (back-drive friction would help).
Preload is an ideal torque law; real spring geometry, hysteresis and attachment not designed.
Reflected rotor inertia 3e-6 kg m2 is the package assumption; post-cut gearbox torque is sensitive to it.
Cut modeled as ideal and instantaneous at -3.5 deg (no switch hysteresis or latency).
pluginFriction: rotary-holding (7e1ed2d) still rejects zero free travel and has no preload, soft-stop impact or drive-cut duty; built project-side again.
